title: PowerShell process uses an encoded-command flag
description: Detects PowerShell command lines containing a delimited encoded-command flag and Base64-shaped argument. Encoding is common in management tools; the argument is not decoded and the event alone does not establish malicious execution.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may use an encoded PowerShell command to obscure execution content.
hypothesis.rationale: Encoded PowerShell is frequently used to conceal commands, but administrators, deployment systems, and security products can also use the feature legitimately.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify documented encoded-command flag forms and common abbreviations while excluding EncodedArguments, encoding-related names and flags without a value.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Decode the command safely and determine whether its origin, user, process tree, and subsequent behavior match an approved administrative workflow.
steps: Preserve the original command line and decode the supplied value in an isolated analysis workflow without executing it.
Review the parent process, account, device, script origin, signer, and related file or network activity.
Confirm an approved automation or change record; otherwise contain the endpoint and investigate the account and process tree.
false_positives: Approved software deployment, endpoint management, security tooling, and administrative automation

validation.expected_outcome: Match delimited encoded-command flags with a Base64-shaped value, including whitespace and case variants; do not treat encoding as proof of malicious execution.

limitations: Encoded PowerShell is common in administration. This is a low-confidence hunt signal; payload decoding and contextual correlation are required.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
